Alternaria_Blotch.quote: Symptoms on leaves appear as brown to purplish irregular spots surrounded by a black border.
Alternaria leaf blotch and fruit spot

Apple_Scab.quote: Lesions on the leaf first appear as light green circular spots that later become olive green and velvety in appearance.
Symptoms on the fruit appear as distinct, almost circular lesions that are olive-green and velvety at first, but later become darker, scabby, and sometimes cracked.

Black_Rot.quote: The first signs of black rot are small, purple spots appearing on the upper surfaces of leaves and enlarging into circles 1/8 to 1/4 inch in diameter.
Infected areas on mature fruit become black, are irregular in shape, and are occasionally surrounded by a red halo.
Cankers appear as a sunken, reddish-brown area on infected branches.

Brown_Spot.quote: Marssonina leaf spots first appear on the upper surface of mature leaves. The irregularly-shaped spots are grayish-brown with a purple border and are 1/8th to 3/8th inch-diameter.
On fruit, Marssonina first causes depressed brown lesions, which eventually turn black at harvest.

Cedar_Apple_Rust.quote: One to two weeks after infection, yellow spots will appear on the tops of the leaves, which can increase in size up to 1/4 inch and will have a rusty appearance.
The rust causes yellow to orange spots similar to those found on the leaves, but the spots are usually much larger.

Grey_Spot.quote: Foliage symptoms are characterized by light gray spots with a dark dot in the center.
Shiny, black blotches develop on fruit with irregular edges and radiating outgrowths.

Powdery_Mildew.quote: On leaves of new shoot growth, symptoms of powdery mildew are feltlike, white patches on the margins and lower surfaces.
The infected shoots have a silver-gray appearance and may exhibit defoliation, stunted growth, and die-back.
When fruits are infected, a network of lines, generally referred to as russetting, develops on the skin in the diseased area.
